### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a867bd2f52bdd1bbc527567919f8a99fb9d7fa78` — the merge of head `8f2c22d91d14b0b8fb2c6693b349b7759dd60213` into base `1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a867bd2f52bdd1bbc527567919f8a99fb9d7fa78 && git checkout a867bd2f52bdd1bbc527567919f8a99fb9d7fa78
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 8f2c22d91d14b0b8fb2c6693b349b7759dd60213 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 && git merge --no-ff 8f2c22d91d14b0b8fb2c6693b349b7759dd60213

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f2c22d91d14b0b8fb2c6693b349b7759dd60213`
Local-runs: probe — the dispatching brief asked for the touched packages' suites on this head; both were run in a scratch worktree, with one route ablation and read-only probes of the stored-row shape
Scope: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts

First full review of this head. Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and on the changeset). The diff touches no published schema and no governed rule text. This record stays at the rule layer, as `security-findings.md` section 6 requires.

### ① Derived judgments

- The rule the PR states is the one public card 33282 rules: an action is identified by owner, owning object and name; binding first, then owner; the declaration a route judges and the handler it runs are one item's.
- Registry: a package-less action registration no longer replaces a package-less action of another owner key. Every reader that asked the bare slot through `bareSlotEntriesOf` now sees each key's item, and the bound-action fold (`boundServedActions`) lists the other key's item. What one registration replaces is a subset of what it replaced on `main` (its own key, and a stored row's earlier stored row), so no single-item answer moves; the two controls pin that.
- Route: the bare route, the registry fallback rung and the environment address each take the package-less item on the route's own key; beside one package holder the bound rung's platform item is served. A route with no declaration is refused by the door (`action-dispatch.ts`, the undeclared refusal), so every cell that still answers no declaration is the refusing direction.
- The two-holder cell keeps the answer an earlier ruling pinned (no declaration); the PR body and the handoff both say so, and the pin is in the new describe.
- CI on this head: every check run is `success` or `skipped`; none failed, none pending.
- Local, on this head: `@objectstack/objectql` 596 files, 13142 tests passed (the PR body's count). `@objectstack/runtime` 603 files, 10918 passed and 19 skipped (the PR body's count). The two touched test files alone: 34 and 148 passed. With the route's own-key pick disabled, 3 of the 12 route pins go red (the two bound-route cases beside no holder, and the environment-address case) and the other 145 of the file's 148 stay green; the source was restored and the worktree is clean.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, value or type is added, removed or re-meant; the docs already teach bound before object-less. `none` takes `patch`, and both packages carry `patch`.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is declared on both carriers with the same wording. The narrowing is BREAKING and the changeset carries the banner, the FROM and TO mapping, and the ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition. The added `SchemaRegistry.getEnvironmentScopedActions` and the optional member on `PackageScopedRegistry` are additive.
- `Skills-docs: none` carries its reason and the reason matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay author to name.
- Independence: the PR was dispatched by `security#1` (another account) and implemented on its branch. Stated for the record: public card 33282, whose ruling is this order's rule, was filed by this account from another seat's session. This account neither dispatched nor implemented the diff.
- No SQL is added; the new reads are in-memory registry reads. The route adds one more full listing of the registry's actions on the path that already lists them once (N3).
- No file outside the declared surface is touched. The draft state, the labels and the queue are left as they are.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published contract on `main`: it takes no declared capability away. The docs already state that a route reaches the action bound to its object before an object-less one; the narrowed cell is the one where `main` answered by registration order, and the PR makes the documented order the answer in both orders. The requirements a caller must hold on that route are the served item's own, which is the spec's own refusal made real.

Per file:

- `registry.ts`: the keep rule, the removal rule and the bare-slot promotion agree with the changeset's three sentences. The owner-key slot mark cannot be read as a bare key, a composite key or a package overlay slot by any of the key scans I read.
- `action-package-addressing.ts`, `package-scoped-resolver.ts`: the owner-key view reads its own key's item; a registry without the new member reads as before.
- `action-execution.ts`: the pick follows the order `actionHandlerObjectKeys` reaches a handler in, so declaration and handler are one item's on every pinned route; it stands aside whenever the answer is a package's item, the route's key already matches, or the rung holds anything but one item.
- Tests: 6 registry cases and 12 route cases, each cell in both registration orders, controls marked. The pin the card asked for (the bound item's requirements gate the bound route, both orders, beside 0 and 1 holders) is there and goes red under the ablation above.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (accepted deviations; none changes the verdict):

- N1 (nit): the route pins beside package holders model the environment's item without the stored-row stamp, as the describe's own docblock says. The stamped shape is pinned at the registry level only. I probed the stamped shape on the route beside no holder, in both orders: the declared answers hold. A stamped route pin beside no holder is a cheap follow-up.
- N2 (nit): one adjacent composition outside the declared cells still answers by registration order, in the refusing direction only. Detail goes to the security seat, not here.
- N3 (nit): the route's new pick lists every registered action a second time per call on the by-name path.
- N4 (nit): readers that name no object (`getItem`, the by-name unregister) still address whichever package-less item sits in the bare slot; the code comments say so, the changeset does not. No route reads them for a gate.

Implemented-by: `claude/package-less-action-two-keys`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cy7hQ5MvQ83ByNZ8ZH`

**VERDICT: PASS**
